guides.terms: New to Tinnitus? What to Do First, and What to Expect | Tinnitus Evidence Just noticed ringing in your ears? What helps in the first days and weeks, the few warning signs that need quick help, and an honest answer to whether it goes away. Hearing a sound no one else can hear can be frightening, especially at first. You are not alone: about 1 in 7 adults has some tinnitus, and it is usually not a sign of anything serious. guides.desc: Explaining tinnitus, and how loved ones can help
guides.terms: Tinnitus and Family: How to Explain It and How Loved Ones Can Help | Tinnitus Evidence Tinnitus affects the whole household. A 30-second way to explain it, what helps and what doesn't for partners and family, home tips, children, and what to do if you're worried. Tinnitus doesn't only affect the person who hears it. guides.title: Sound sensitivity and hearing protection
guides.desc: When sounds feel too loud, and protecting your ears
guides.terms: Hyperacusis and Hearing Protection: When Sounds Feel Too Loud | Tinnitus Evidence Everyday sounds too loud or painful? How to protect your ears without over-protecting, how to fit earplugs, iPhone settings, help that works, and when to get checked. Many people with tinnitus also find some everyday sounds too loud or uncomfortable. It's tempting to block everything out, but over-protecting your ears can make sensitivity worse. The aim is to protect your ears from truly loud sound, and gently get used to everyday sound again. What's going on? Protect, or don't plug?
